category_name: Socio-technical community smells and quality phenomena
definition: Quality-relevant phenomena explicitly observed in software-development communities or repository social structures, including community smells and interaction or organizational anti-patterns. These phenomena remain distinct from code defects, runtime failures, and causal claims about software quality.

A software-generation or automated-transformation mechanism produces an artifact that source evidence shows to be syntactically invalid, semantically invalid, structurally invalid, incomplete, non-executable, or otherwise outside its declared supported validity conditions.
An analytical macro-group for explicitly deliberate fault construction, consisting of items whose frozen evidence nature is SYNTHETIC_INJECTED or MUTATION_OPERATOR.

category_name: Syntactic or compilation invalidity of generated/transformed artifacts
definition: A generated or automatically transformed artifact is reported as syntactically invalid, rejected by compilation, unable to compile, or otherwise failing an explicit syntactic/compilation validity condition.

category_name: Automatically generated or transformed software artifact
definition: A software artifact explicitly produced by an automated generation, synthesis, repair, compilation, transpilation, translation, or model-transformation mechanism.
The source-scoped program, source fragment or circuit instance whose condition/behavior is at issue; preserve its actual representation level.
The identified software implementation/component of an SDK, simulator, compiler or analysis tool that exhibits the source-described issue.
The testing workflow, harness, oracle facility or supporting test code whose adequacy/capability is the affected object.

category_name: Reported output, verdict or diagnostic object
definition: A source-identified output/distribution, statistical verdict or diagnostic record considered as the affected/result object at the stated abstraction level.
The software model/design representation explicitly involved in the source problem, including produced models when actual production is supported.
An explicitly supported syntactic-invalidity or syntax-rejection outcome at the source-defined stage.
A reported compiler/transpiler-stage failure or error that prevents the intended continuation/execution, without presuming syntax is the failure criterion.

A source-described failure while using/executing a software facility: exception, API failure, crash, hang, aborted operation or resource-bounded noncompletion, with stage/condition qualifiers where stated.
A reported deviation of outputs, distributions, traces or prediction results from a stated reference/specification/criterion within its scope.
Source-supported measured or analytically modeled deviation from the stated numerical/reference quantity under explicit assumptions.
Source-reported variability/intermittence of a test/program outcome in the recorded context.
An explicitly reported warning/diagnostic or assessed quality-indicator outcome, without asserting a confirmed underlying defect.

category_name: Program, state, or dependency consistency problem
definition: A source-supported problem in a program-required state/use/operation/dependency relation, retaining the precise initialization, operand/control, measurement or lifetime condition where actually established.

A source-supported underlying numerical or computational stability problem, such as approximation/precision or stability of computation under stated conditions; numerical deviation as symptom alone is insufficient.
A source-supported software robustness/security weakness relative to its declared task, similarity, confidentiality or protection criterion.

category_name: Structural, design, representation, or integration adequacy problem
definition: A source-supported underlying structural, design, representation or integration adequacy problem in a software structure, design organization, representation correspondence/abstraction or interface relationship.
A source-supported mismatch/limitation in analysis precision, test criteria or diagnostic assessment relative to the stated intended judgment.

Substantive static V&V mechanisms that inspect source code, models, intermediate representations, configuration/design artifacts, or related software artifacts without requiring execution of the target program. The mechanism performs substantive analysis/checking of a property, rule, defect condition, consistency condition, structural relation, or equivalent V&V-relevant characteristic. Static analysis and linting retain their source-supported child distinctions.
Higher-level synthesis family grouping formal verification/proof mechanisms and symbolic reasoning mechanisms while preserving their original specific technique_class.

Validation mechanisms that determine correctness, success or failure through at least one explicit assertion, state predicate, output predicate, acceptance predicate, statistical decision criterion, or threshold/pass-fail rule with an actual validation role. Preserve assertion-based and statistical-oracle distinctions; measurement without source-supported decision logic is not sufficient.
Tentative higher-level family drawn from explicit frozen technique classifications, with original specific class preserved.

category_name: Test generation, selection, and guided exploration
definition: Techniques whose substantive testing mechanism actively generates, searches for, selects, prioritizes, reduces, fuzzes, combines, or adaptively explores test inputs, test cases, test configurations, stimuli, or equivalent testing candidates. Preserve distinct generation, selection and exploration mechanisms; active coverage guidance is one mechanism, not a requirement for all test selection.

category_name: Coverage adequacy criteria without generation feedback
definition: Coverage definitions or measurements for testing adequacy where coverage feedback does not actively guide generation, selection, prioritization or exploration.
Criteria that partition the quantum input-state space or prescribe representative input states for testing, without by themselves constituting an automated test-generation mechanism.
Learned mechanisms that filter, compensate, denoise, condition, or otherwise adapt noisy quantum execution evidence to support a testing oracle or correctness decision.

Validation of correspondence between source artifacts and generated or derived models, including mapped, missing, irrelevant, or mismatched elements and relationships within the declared transformation scope.
A workflow that reproduces a buggy failure, verifies behavior of a developer-fixed/reference version, and reuses an executable task-specific oracle to assess fixes or repairs.
Direct validation of generated component functionality against an explicit truth-table specification within the source-supported basis-state/component scope.
Testing explicitly scoped by the source to an individual unit/module/function/component or equivalent unit-level artifact.
Testing explicitly scoped by the source to interactions or integration among multiple software/components/subsystems.
Testing explicitly scoped by the source to end-to-end or complete-system behavior.

A representation used primarily as internal machinery for implementation, compilation, analysis, detection, diagnosis, or transformation, without sufficient source evidence that it is proposed as a substantive software-modeling abstraction.
A source-defined metamodel or modeling profile that explicitly structures software/model entities, relationships, properties, constraints, or stereotypes for quantum or hybrid software.

A source-defined programming, modeling, domain-specific, or specification language whose constructs explicitly represent quantum/hybrid software entities, operations, relationships, properties, or behavioral semantics.
A source-defined abstraction that explicitly represents program semantics, quantum/classical state, state relations, abstract interpretation domains, or semantic program behavior.

A source-defined representation whose primary role is to express software/system requirements, feature choices, configuration options, variability, selection criteria, or related constraints for quantum or hybrid software.

A representation whose explicit source-supported role is to describe test cases, test spaces, test specifications, test environments, testing concepts, contracts, assertions, or related V&V artifacts.

A representation that explicitly describes software or system components, layers, interfaces, deployment/execution elements, dependencies, or architectural relationships in quantum or hybrid software.
A representation that explicitly describes development phases, activities, roles, artifacts, transitions, feedback loops, or software-engineering workflow.

A source-supported representation of program, source, or intermediate program objects in which meaningful program-level organization, dependencies, relations, mappings, structure, or transformations are themselves represented as substantive software/program information rather than merely as internal implementation machinery.

A representation whose explicit source-supported purpose is to express, enable, organize or communicate analysis or reasoning about software/program structure, behavior, properties, dependencies or semantics, beyond merely serving as private/internal machinery of an analysis tool.

A representation whose explicit source-supported purpose is to mediate or support transformation, translation, modernization, exchange, conversion, interoperability or bridging between program/model/representation forms or software/system contexts.
A representation whose explicit source-supported purpose is to support, organize, configure, mediate or represent execution/runtime behavior or runtime interaction.
